previous_description: Structured log record in the OTel data model, capturing an event with dual timestamps (timeUnixNano for event occurrence, observedTimeUnixNano for ingestion), a 1–24 severity scale, and an unstructured body. Supports trace context correlation to link logs to distributed traces.
definition: A structured log event emitted by application or library code through a logging API or the OTel Logs Bridge API. It is identified by a stable message template or event name together with its severity, body and attributes. It models the kind of record a log call site produces, not a transient annotation on a span.

distinguish_from.when: the occurrence is recorded on an active span via span.addEvent or span.recordException, rather than emitted through a logger as an independent record
the code sets up the LoggerProvider, its exporters or its minimum-severity filtering, rather than emitting a particular log event
the code filters, enriches, batches or routes log records in the pipeline instead of producing them
the occurrence is counted or measured as an aggregated numeric time series instead of being recorded as an individual event with a body

standard_reference: OpenTelemetry Logs Data Model – LogRecord (Log and Event Record Definition)
code_evidence: A structured logger call with a stable message template or event name plus key-value fields, e.g. logger.warn('payment.declined', {orderId, reason}) or log.info().addKeyValue(...)
A direct OTel Logs Bridge API emission such as logger.emit({severityNumber, severityText, body, attributes}) or LogRecordBuilder.setBody(...).emit()
Documented log or audit event catalogs, or constants enumerating log event names and their fields, e.g. AUDIT_USER_LOGIN = 'user.login' referenced from logging calls

attribute_descriptions.name: timeUnixNano
attribute_descriptions.description: Time the described event occurred, given as nanoseconds since the Unix epoch encoded as a decimal string; set it when the emitting source supplies an event time, otherwise use '0' (unknown).

attribute_descriptions.name: observedTimeUnixNano
attribute_descriptions.description: Time the record was observed by the collection pipeline (SDK or collector), given as nanoseconds since the Unix epoch encoded as a decimal string; it is normally set by the pipeline and falls back to timeUnixNano when no separate observation time exists.

attribute_descriptions.name: severityNumber
attribute_descriptions.description: OTel numeric severity from 1 to 24 (1–4 TRACE, 5–8 DEBUG, 9–12 INFO, 13–16 WARN, 17–20 ERROR, 21–24 FATAL), with 0 meaning unspecified; set it to the level used by the emitting call.

attribute_descriptions.name: severityText
attribute_descriptions.description: Original severity label as produced by the source logging framework (e.g., 'WARNING', 'err'); set it to preserve the native level name alongside severityNumber.

attribute_descriptions.name: body
attribute_descriptions.description: The log message or event payload, typically the message template (e.g., 'Order {orderId} created') or a serialized structured body; set it to the stable content that identifies this record.

attribute_descriptions.name: flags
attribute_descriptions.description: W3C trace flags byte from the span context active at emission, as a hex string (e.g., '01' = sampled); set it when the record is correlated with a trace, otherwise use '00'.

attribute_descriptions.name: droppedAttributesCount
attribute_descriptions.description: Number of attributes discarded because of attribute count or length limits, as a non-negative integer; use 0 for modelled records unless limits are known to truncate them.

notes: The type lacks traceId and spanId, so the claimed trace correlation is not expressible; it also lacks eventName. severityNumber should be an integer constrained to 0–24. The required instance-level fields (timestamps, flags) conflict with modelling design-time log event types. Consider making them optional, or splitting the type into a log event definition versus a record instance.
